claims.statement: The manual recommends beans with a 'Roasted On' date used 5 to 20 days after roasting; stale beans run fast.
Dose so the tamper's metal cap sits level with the basket rim after tamping, and tamp firmly.
On the Express the steam light flashes while the machine heats for steam, and it purges water into the drip tray after shots and steaming.
The manual lists a coarse grind, too small a dose and too light a tamp as the causes of a shot running too fast, and does not list the machine.
The Express built-in grinder has 16 settings; the Pro's has 30 settings with Baratza burrs.
The Dual Boiler has no grinder in either market, so a standalone grinder is needed if you move to it.
In a 2026 owner thread, replies said the Express's biggest bottleneck is the grinder, and that a dual boiler is worth it mainly for milk drinkers tired of the steaming wait.
Express brew temperature can be adjusted up to 4°F either way in 2°F steps in Advanced Temperature Mode.
Barista Pro shot temperature can be adjusted from the SHOT TEMP menu.
The Express heats with a single thermocoil.
A retailer comparison and an independent review both say the Express cannot brew and steam at the same time.
The Dual Boiler brews and steams at the same time, with PID-controlled boilers.
The Oracle Dual Boiler's dual boilers let it steam while it brews, with PID temperature control.
The Barista Pro's ThermoJet is listed with a 3-second heat-up, and its manual describes steaming after a short purge with no heat-up wait.
The original Oracle is listed as discontinued in the US.
The Oracle Jet grinds, doses and tamps automatically into a 58 mm portafilter, textures milk hands-free, and heats with a ThermoJet rather than boilers.
The Oracle Dual Boiler automates grind, dose, tamp and milk, uses a 58 mm portafilter, and its grinder adjusts automatically.
Owners of the original Oracle called its built-in grinder 'a bit meh', said grinds after the first come out coarser on back-to-back drinks, and some kept an external grinder.
Weak or no steam, shots that only drip and coffee that isn't hot enough are listed as descale symptoms in the manual's troubleshooting table.
The Express comes with a 54 mm portafilter; the Dual Boiler uses a 58 mm portafilter.
The DF54 is a single-dose grinder with 54 mm flat burrs and stepless adjustment.
A reader of a DF54 review says its cradle is designed for 58 mm portafilters and a 54 mm one can be pushed in and held.
The reviewer recommends UK buyers buy the DF54 from a UK seller, warning of EU plugs, no UK warranty and import fees from overseas sellers.

Dual Boiler owners report mixed reliability: repairs after three and eight years, level-probe failures, a steam leak damaging a control board, a repairer suggesting a service every two years, and others calling it solid.
